posts.title: Taiwan voters flaunt their political colours ahead of local polls
posts.description: Taiwanese voters are displaying their political colours like never before, adorning themselves, their shops and even their pets with ribbons to show fervent support for their favourite candidates ahead of Saturday’s local elections . Incumbent Taipei mayor Chiang Wan-an of Kuomintang holds an election eve rally on November 27 ahead of a close race to keep his job against challenger Puma Shen of the Democratic Progressive Party. Photo: Chiang Wan-an, via Facebook. Grassroots campaigning has intensified in the run-up to the vote, which will decide races for around 11,000 posts, including mayors and magistrates, across 22 cities and counties. While giveaways have been a feature of previous campaigns, voters have taken it to a new level this year. In Taipei, where the mayoral contest looks set to go down to the wire, people have been designing, making and sharing ribbons to promote their preferred candidate. posts.title: China critic Puma Shen in close election race for Taipei mayor
posts.description: Taiwanese people lined up at polling stations across Taipei on Saturday to cast their ballots in a tight race for mayor, as voting got underway in local elections across the island democracy. Taipei mayor candidate Puma Shen, a vocal China critic, meets village chiefs in the lead up to the local election. Photo: Puma Shen, via Threads. China critic Puma Shen is seeking to flip what has long been considered a safe seat for the Kuomintang party (KMT), which favours closer ties with Beijing, and become the capital’s first Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) mayor in nearly 30 years. Taiwan’s local elections are held every four years and will decide races for about 11,000 positions, including mayors and magistrates, across the island democracy’s 22 cities and counties. posts.title: Hong Kong’s top court quashes autistic man’s conviction for flag desecration citing his condition
posts.description: Hong Kong’s top court has quashed an autistic man’s conviction for flag desecration, ruling that medical evidence showed he may have been affected by conditions characterised by hypersensitivity to visual stimuli. China and Hong Kong flags at Central Market on Oct. 1, 2022. File photo: Lea Mok/HKFP. The Court of Final Appeal on Friday ruled in favour of Wong Chun-lok, overturning his conviction for desecrating China’s national flag and the Hong Kong regional flag on National Day, October 1, 2022. Wong, who was 19 at the time and had been diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder during childhood, stood accused of desecrating one national flag and four Hong Kong flags on National Day in Sham Shui Po by bending their flagpoles. He denied the charges, saying he was triggered by the bright colours of the flags. A magistrate found him guilty and sentenced him to detention in a rehabilitation centre in June 2023.
